findings.description: As the sound of an exterior door opening plays, the customer enters the diner by walking out from the doorway behind the counter next to the kitchen pass-through rather than from an entrance in the customer area.

When the waitress pours coffee into the mug, the glass carafe remains nearly horizontal with the liquid level flat and well below the spout, yet a stream of coffee pours straight down through the front of the pot.

At 00:32–00:44 (while it is dark outside), the plate of toast and eggs is already sitting on the counter in front of the man. At 01:00 (after sunrise), the plate has vanished from the counter, and at 01:09 the waitress brings out the same plate to serve him again, which he then declines.
Through the window behind the waitress (left of center), a semi-truck on the road moves smoothly from left to right trailer-first, travelling backwards at highway speed.

Two hands enter from opposite sides of the frame to place money on the counter, and as the right hand slides across the bills, the top note morphs from a '1' denomination into a '100' denomination with a distorted portrait.

The waitress's reflection in the window shows her torso and hanging glasses facing toward the camera at an impossible angle relative to her body, and when she lowers her head and turns away at 01:48–01:49, her reflection remains frozen staring straight ahead.

As the waitress stands up from the stool and walks behind the counter on the right, an identical duplicate of the waitress (same blue shirt, white apron, hair bun, and glasses on a lanyard) materializes in the background near the kitchen window, leaving two copies of her in the scene simultaneously.
